2462 ḗka 'one' RV. 2. Replaced by * ēkka- either with emph. doubling (as in Pk. igga -) or as MIA. loan from
Sk. when single - k - was no longer a sound of the language. 1. Pa. ēka - 'one', °aka - 'single'; Aś. shah. man. gir.
jau. eka -, sn. ika - 'one'; NiDoc. eka , ega ; Pk. ēga - (emph. Ap. egga -), ēa -, iga - (emph. igga -); Ash. a 'one,
a', ač 'one', Kt. ew , Wg. ew , εw (NTS xvii 234 < * ēō < ēká -, not * ēva -, Av. aēva -), Pr. ipǖ́n (+?); Paš. ẹ̄ , ī 'one, alone'; Kho. i 'one', Tor. ē 'one, a'; N. yeuṭā 'one', A. eṭā (+ vr̥tta - ? cf. ēkavŕ̥t - 'single' AV.); Or. e 'one, only'. 2.
